title: Glencore begins trading on Australian Securities Exchange
text: Back to News GlencoreMedia and Insights...NewsGlencore begins trading on Australian Securities Exchangeposted:14/10/2026Glencore begins trading on Australian Securities ExchangeShareShareGlencore plc Baar, Switzerland 14 October 2026Glencore has begun trading on the Australian Securities Exchange (ASX) under the ASX code GLC*.Gary Nagle, Glencore’s CEO, said it was an exciting day for the company. “Glencore has been investing in Australia for decades and we know the Australian investment community has a sophisticated understanding of global resources and commodity markets,” said Mr Nagle.Glencore is one of the world’s largest globally diversified natural resource companies that produces and markets more than 60 commodities which advance everyday life.  We have 140,000 employees and contractors working across our operations in over 30 countries. We produce, process, recycle, source, market and distribute the commodities that support growing energy demand and security, continued urbanisation, the energy transition and AI infrastructure.Glencore has a primary listing in London and an existing secondary listing in Johannesburg, with US$28.7 billion of announced shareholder returns since 2021, which represents about one-third of the company’s market cap. “We believe our portfolio of mainly brownfield copper growth projects provides us with a clear pathway to become one of the world’s largest copper producers.  In addition, our traditional bulk operations, including steel making and energy coal, along with our leading marketing business has consistently generated sizeable cash flows” said Mr Nagle, who noted that copper, in particular, is essential to everything from power grids and renewable energy to electric vehicles and AI data centres.The ASX listing deepens Glencore’s 30-year commitment to Australia.  Glencore is one of Australia’s largest and most diverse resources companies, with 16,820 employees and contractors across 16 active mining operations and seven metals processing facilities.Glencore is Australia’s largest producer of coal, cobalt, nickel, lead and zinc.  The Glencore Technology business offers a range of mineral processing technology solutions to global smelters and refineries, and Glencore’s oil business is one of the largest importers of liquid fuels (including diesel) into Australia contributing to national fuel security.“We are very proud of the important economic contribution we make in Australia,” said Mr Nagle. “Over the past five years, Glencore has directly contributed A$95 billion to the Australian economy, including support for more than 6,440 Australian-based businesses and payment of over A$24 billion in taxes and royalties to Australian governments.”* Each producer and marketer of more than 60 commodities. Through a network of assets, customers and suppliers that spans the globe, we produce, process, recycle, source, market and distribute the commodities that advance everyday life. With over 140,000 employees and contractors and a strong footprint in over 30 countries in both established and emerging regions for natural resources, our marketing and industrial activities are supported by a global network of offices.Glencore’s customers are principally industrial consumers, such as those in the automotive, steel, power generation, battery manufacturing and oil sectors. We also provide financing, logistics and other services to producers and consumers of commodities. About Glencore Australia In Australia, Glencore produces coal, zinc, nickel, cobalt, lead and silver from 16 active mining operations. We also operate seven copper, zinc, lead, nickel and cobalt processing assets in Queensland, Western Australia and the Northern Territory, including concentrators, smelters and refineries.We are among Australia’s largest producers and marketers of natural resources, connecting Australian resources with industrial customers around the world. Through our diverse portfolio, we responsibly supply the resources that advance everyday life.In 2025 Glencore spent A$19.3 billion operating in Australia, providing jobs for 16,820 people and making a significant socio-economic contribution across the country. This included spending A$14.21 billion with 6,440 businesses, as well as A$2.4 billion in government tax and royalty payments.We are committed to providing a safe, inclusive and respectful workplace for our people, to respecting the environment, to engaging openly and constructively with the Traditional Owners on whose lands we operate and to bringing value to local communities.For more information, visit www.glencore.com.auImportant information  This material does not purport to contain all of the information you may wish to consider.
